# Meridian — Full LLM Context

Generated: 2026-07-25. Reconciled against measured reality: 2026-07-26.

Durable full-context map and operating contract for LLM agents working in
`github.com/madfam-org/meridian`. This file is tool-agnostic: it does not depend
on any vendor-specific instruction format.

---

## Purpose

Give an agent a stable map of what this repository is, what is actually built,
what must never be broken, and how to verify a change — without reading the
whole tree first.

## Canonical instruction order

1. `AGENTS.md` — canonical agent operating instructions.
2. `packages/core/src/` — the shared contract. All of it, about 1,160 lines
   across nine modules. Its doc comments explain *why* each type is shaped the
   way it is.
3. `README.md` — honest status, architecture, quickstart, repository map.
4. `ECOSYSTEM.md` — ecosystem position, domain layout, and Enclii day-to-day.
5. `docs/` — PRD, architecture, regulatory and commercial posture, catalog
   review, counsel packet, personas, dated research notes, ADRs.
6. The specific package `src/` you are changing.

`AGENTS.md` is the source of truth. `CLAUDE.md` exists only to redirect Claude
and other legacy agent integrations to it.

---

## What this repository is

A platform for the end-to-end migration lifecycle:

- **Eligibility** — assessment against a versioned, citation-backed catalog of
  immigration pathways.
- **Documents** — sequential assembly with apostille / consular legalisation
  routing and sworn-translation requirements, with freshness projected to the
  submission date.
- **Identity** — machine-readable travel-document validation to ICAO Doc 9303.
- **Presence** — continuous cross-border day counting: tax residency, Schengen
  90/180, continuous-residence clocks, qualifying-work accumulation.
- **Coverage** — a registry of the whole problem, so how much of it is solved
  can be measured rather than asserted.

Three corridors seed the catalog: **Mexico → Spain**, **Mexico → Canada** and
**Mexico → United States**. The engine is jurisdiction-generic; the corridors
are data.

**Pillar**: Mobility. **Visibility**: PUBLIC. **Licence**: AGPL-3.0-only.
**Owner**: Innovaciones MADFAM S.A.S. de C.V., Cuernavaca, Morelos, Mexico.

---

Twelve workspace projects — eight libraries under `packages/`, four deployables
under `apps/`. `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` exits clean in all twelve. Whole-repo
through turbo: `pnpm typecheck` 19/19 tasks, `pnpm test` 19/19, `pnpm build`
12/12.

**All three Next.js applications now have test suites.** Until 2026-07-26 they
had no test file at all, and that was the largest gap in the repository. What
they assert is rendering and state derivation — the arithmetic a page shows a
reader, the locale a document is served in, the disclosure notice that must
accompany an assessment — not browser automation. These counts were still moving
while this file was written; get them from `pnpm test` rather than from here.

### Present and passing

Four policy guards run clean, and each reports what it examined rather than only
its verdict:

```
check-advice-boundary:       OK — gate and producer anchors verified,
                             233 application files read, 16 routes examined
check-no-credential-custody: OK — 454 files scanned, 3 rules,
                             3 path exemptions, 2 structural anchors verified
check-pathway-citations:     OK — as of 2026-07-26: 15 catalog files, 84 pathways,
                             378 citations, 1094 criterion references resolved
check-workspace-manifests:   OK — 12 workspace projects present in all 4
                             Dockerfiles and in the lockfile
```

The citations check prints the UTC date it ran on, because citation staleness is
measured against it. The file counts in the first two move as the tree grows —
they read 185 and 400 earlier the same day, before the application tests landed
— which is exactly why each guard reports what it examined: a guard you cannot
catch reading nothing is a guard that agrees with everything.

An earlier revision of the root documents recorded this check as *failing*:
the catalog index had moved
from a literal array to a list of modules and the guard could not locate the
shipped set, so its anti-vacuity check refused to confirm a set it could not
read. It was re-anchored on the new shape rather than relaxed.

`scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs` is a fifth script and is **not** a guard. It prints
the coverage arithmetic with its own denominator and caveats, reads the built
objects from `packages/atlas/dist` rather than parsing source, and takes
`--strict` to exit non-zero when the atlas has integrity findings. It is not in
CI.

CI at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — jobs `policy` (the four guards, before any
install), `typecheck`, `test`, `build` — plus `build-deploy.yml`, which builds
and signs four images. Deployment configuration: `enclii.yaml` (five YAML
documents: a project-level record plus one Service per deployable),
`Dockerfile.{api,web,admin,landing}`, `docker-compose.yml` (Postgres only, for
local development), `infra/k8s/production/` (namespace, four deployment/service
pairs, kustomization, and a secrets template that is deliberately not a
kustomize resource).

### Deployed

Observed 2026-07-26 by requesting each hostname:

| Service | Hostname | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `meridian-landing` | meridian.madfam.io | `200`; `/` English, `/es` Spanish, `/en` `308`s to `/` |
| `meridian-app` | meridian-app.madfam.io | `200` |
| `meridian-admin` | meridian-admin.madfam.io | `200` |
| `meridian-api` | meridian-api.madfam.io | `502` — the tunnel answers, no origin does |

The three Next applications read no API host from their environment, so nothing
they render depends on the API. "Live" here means *serving pages*, not *end to
end*: no request has travelled from a screen through the service to a database
in any environment.

### The API, as built

`apps/api` is a real Fastify application with a composition root and a suite:

- `src/main.ts` — the only file that reads `process.env`, constructs a database
  client or binds a socket. Loads the Prisma client through a *variable*
  specifier so `tsc --noEmit` does not depend on `prisma generate` having run.
  Shutdown drains in-flight requests before releasing the database, so an audit
  append in progress is not lost.
- `src/config.ts` — validates the whole environment once and reports **every**
  problem in one error. With an empty environment it names seven variables —
  `DATABASE_URL`, `JANUA_JWKS_URL`, `JANUA_ISSUER`, `JANUA_AUDIENCE`, `PORT`,
  `NODE_ENV`, `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` — and exits 78 without printing a value.
  `Dockerfile.api` sets `NODE_ENV` and `PORT`, so a bare `docker run` of the
  image names the remaining five.
- `auth/` — Janua JWKS verification, RS256 checked before **and** during
  verification, issuer and audience both required.
- `disclosure/` — the gate (re-checks a downgraded value), the envelope, a leak
  detector, a Fastify plugin.
- `routes/registry.ts` — an `onRoute` hook that refuses to register any route
  not declaring whether it returns engine output.
- `repositories/` — ports with **structural tenant scoping** (no method takes a
  tenant id; a repository comes from `forTenant()`), Prisma and memory adapters.
- `audit/` — append-only: `append` and `list`, nothing else.
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — 10 models, 15 enums. `prisma/migrations/` holds an
  initial migration; **nothing in the deploy path runs it**, and it has never
  been applied to a live Postgres.
- `routes/` — health, tenants, applicants, matters, tasks, presence, documents,
  pathways, identity, govtech, audit: 41 HTTP routes across 11 modules. The
  identity route returns an MRZ verdict and persists none of the document.
- The readiness probe distinguishes *unreachable*, *reachable but no schema* and
  *healthy*, and says which. It used to be `SELECT 1`, which proves a socket and
  not a schema: against a schema-less database it returned ready, the pod would
  have joined the Service, and every authenticated request would have 500'd
  inside the auth hook. An empty `tenants` table is a legitimate fresh
  deployment and is not confused with a missing one.
- `tests/` — token verification against the attacks actually used against JWT
  APIs, the advice boundary end to end, tenant isolation at the HTTP boundary
  with a valid token for the wrong tenant, readiness with the dependency down,
  and the case-file routes at the Schengen 90/91 boundary. All of them run over
  `InMemoryRepositoryProvider`.

The image builds and starts: `docker build -f Dockerfile.api` then `docker run`
reaches configuration validation and exits 78. The build imports every workspace
package under Node before it will emit an image, which is what catches a package
whose `exports` resolve to TypeScript — correct in the workspace, fatal in a
container.

### The applications

All three are Next.js 15 App Router applications routing under `app/[locale]/`.

`apps/landing` — the public marketing site, local dev port 3000, deployed as
`meridian-landing` on `meridian.madfam.io`. It carries **a working Schengen
90/180 calculator on the page itself**: a stranger enters two trips and gets
their own number, with the 180-day window, a per-trip table showing which days
were charged and why each uncharged day was not, the citation, and a statement
of what the number is not. No account, no click-through, no email. It runs in
the browser because the domain packages are pure computation, which is also why
"nothing is transmitted" is a property of the code rather than a promise. Every
published figure is **counted, not written**: `lib/catalog-facts.ts` imports
`@meridian/core` and `@meridian/pathways` and derives pathways shipped,
counsel-reviewed, routes open, criteria, distinct sources cited, how many are
`discretionary`, how many carry a URL and how many have left the freshest
staleness band — all at build time, as at one fixed civil date. The Schengen
thresholds and citation are **imported from `@meridian/presence`**, not copied:
an earlier revision copied them verbatim because the app did not declare that
dependency, and a differential test proved the copies agreed *on the day they
were written*, which is exactly the guarantee that decays. There are no adoption
numbers, no processing-time estimates and no success rates. `output:
'standalone'` is load-bearing: `Dockerfile.landing` copies `.next/standalone`
and fails the build with an explicit message if it is absent.

`apps/web` — applicant portal, port 3001, deployed as `meridian-app`. Routes:
`/`, `/pathways`, `/pathways/[id]`, `/matters`, `/matters/[id]` with `documents`
and `presence` sub-pages, `/tools` with `schengen`, `mrz` and `nationality-es`,
`/pricing`, and `/for` with `/for/[audience]`. The three tools are client-side
and assessment-class: the user's own facts against a cited rule with the
arithmetic shown, nothing transmitted, nothing stored. Schengen surfaces the
Bulgaria/Romania staged-accession window as needing a human rather than
resolving it silently; the nationality check returns indeterminate, as its own
state, when the acquisition mode is unrecorded.

`apps/admin` — firm console, port 3002, deployed as `meridian-admin`. Routes:
`/`, `/matters`, `/matters/[id]`, `/catalog`, `/catalog/[id]`, `/audit`,
`/integrations`, `/representatives`. `MERIDIAN_ASOF` pins its reference date and
`MERIDIAN_ADMIN_DATASET` selects which dataset it serves, falling back visibly
rather than failing the render. Credential types are deliberately **not**
translated where translating them would imply an equivalence between regulators
that does not exist: *abogado colegiado* and *gestor administrativo* are
standard; RCIC and Quebec notary are not translated at all.

None of the three reads an API host from the environment, so none of them calls
the API.

**The gaps, in order of importance:**

1. No contract test suite for the repository ports, which ADR 0006 names as its
   own main risk. The Prisma adapter is covered by `tsc` and nothing else.
2. The migration exists but has never been applied anywhere, and nothing in the
   deploy path runs it.
3. Nothing has been exercised end to end; no request has travelled from a screen
   through the service to a database in any environment.
4. `meridian-api.madfam.io` returns `502`. The operator gates that provision its
   database and its Janua configuration have not all been run.
5. `@meridian/atlas` has no consumer inside the product — it is read by
   `scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs` and by its own tests. The coverage figures are
   reported to us, not to a reader deciding whether Meridian reaches their
   country.
6. `negotiateLocale` is implemented and tested in `@meridian/i18n` and called by
   no application.

### Legal catalog

Counted by loading the built catalog and walking the shipped `Pathway` objects:

- **84 pathways** — 26 Spain, 23 Canada, 35 United States — across **13 source
  modules** in `packages/pathways/src/catalog/`. **0 counsel-reviewed.**
  77 open, 5 closed, 2 suspended. Closed routes stay in the catalog with a
  `closureNote`, because a person already holding that status still needs an
  answer.
- **449 criteria**: 291 `blocking`, 109 `material`, 49 `informational`. 154
  escalate to a human unconditionally and 67 conditionally, so **62 of the 84
  records can only ever return `requires_human_review`** — by design, and each
  escalation names the fact it is waiting for.
- **373 distinct citations** on shipped records; 82 `discretionary`; 347 carry a
  URL. `check-pathway-citations` reports 378 and 1094 because it parses source:
  378 is the count of citation *literals*, five of whose ids are declared twice,
  and 1094 counts every `citationIds` entry anywhere inside a record, of which
  867 sit on criteria and the rest on duration records.
- **63 CUSMA/USMCA professions** in `catalog/cusma-professions.ts`, matching
  8 CFR 214.6(c) which reproduces USMCA Appendix 2 verbatim. That one table
  feeds both the Canadian CUSMA route and the American TN route, so an entry
  dropped from it silently narrows eligibility on two corridors at once. An
  occupation *outside* the Appendix escalates rather than returning "unmet",
  because titles and Appendix entries do not map one to one and "not a listed
  profession" would be a false negative on somebody's livelihood.
- `@meridian/presence`: 6 citations, 3 `discretionary`.
- `@meridian/documents`: 23 citations, 15 `discretionary`.
- `@meridian/govtech`: 16 citations, 9 `discretionary`.
- `verifiedOn` values are `2026-07-25` and `2026-07-26` → `fresh` until
  2026-10-23 at the earliest.

Because nothing is reviewed, `recommend()` returns an empty ranking and lists
all 84 pathways as excluded with code `not_counsel_reviewed`. **That is the
system working.**

Deliberate absences that must not be quietly filled:

- **Asylum, refugee protection and humanitarian/compassionate claims**, in every
  jurisdiction. They turn on credibility assessment rather than criteria, they
  concern people at risk, and a self-serve eligibility checker is the wrong
  instrument.
- **No priority date, visa-bulletin cut-off or wait estimate**, anywhere. The
  Visa Bulletin moves monthly and Mexico is heavily oversubscribed in several
  categories; any number written today is wrong within weeks. The *structure* of
  the limit is stated; the number is not.
- **The US unlawful-presence bars are encoded as "this may apply, ask a
  lawyer"**, never as a verdict. Someone who departs to consular-process can
  trigger a ten-year bar *by departing*, and a confident wrong answer there
  causes exactly the harm the platform exists to prevent.
- **No processing-time estimate on any record.**
- **No Comprehensive Ranking System number of any kind** — no cut-off, no
  maximum, no factor value.
- No operational figure from IRCC's program delivery instructions; canada.ca
  refused automated access throughout the Canadian sweep.

### Coverage — `@meridian/atlas`

The package exists so coverage can be measured rather than asserted, and is
built so the answer cannot be improved by looking away. From
`node scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs --as-of=2026-07-26`:

- **249 jurisdictions** across five region files, deduplicated by ISO 3166-1
  alpha-2, plus **22 mobility agreements**.
- Research status: 123 `stub`, 123 `researched`, 3 `encoded` (CA, ES, US),
  0 `counsel_reviewed`. `researched` means a source was consulted, usually
  establishing only autonomy and bloc membership — it does **not** mean the
  system is mapped.
- **Structural coverage 1.20%** (3 of 249). **Weighted coverage 0.6076%**, where
  covered requires *both* ends encoded — the honest test, since a corridor is
  only as known as its least-known end.
- Destination-side reach, printed explicitly as **not** a coverage figure: 66
  rows carrying 56,078,000 people, 18.4% of world stock.
- Stock table: 280 corridors, 198,645,000 people, **65.34%** of the world total
  of 304,021,813, against a **92.7% ceiling** — 7.3% of world stock is recorded
  against origin "Others" in the UN DESA 2024 bilateral matrix and is
  unattributable in any bilateral source. The cutoff is every country pair at or
  above 200,000 persons.

The denominator errs in both directions and the errors do not cancel: it
*includes* places with no permanent population and no residence route, which
permanently depress structural coverage; it *excludes* roughly seven authorities
that control entry to territory but have no ISO alpha-2 code, each recorded as a
note on the nearest coded entry rather than given an invented key; and three
codes hide more than one control each. A corridor is **derived** from a
destination and an origin, never stored — there is no list of ~40,000 country
pairs, because immigration rules are overwhelmingly destination-side and origin
nationality modifies the terms through blocs and bilateral instruments.

### Government integration capability board

15 declared capabilities across three adapters (`es-clave`, `es-dicireg`,
`ca-ircc`): 6 `available` (**all `local_computation`**), 2 `not_provisioned`,
3 `not_implemented`, 4 `refused_by_policy`, 0 `degraded`, 0 defects.
**Zero `government_system` capabilities are `available`**, and every remote
capability additionally requires an injected transport this repository does not
ship, so `available` is unreachable from inside the package even with every
environment variable set.

---

## The three invariants

Non-negotiable. A change that breaks one is a defect regardless of what else it
improves.

### 1. Never use `Date` for calendar arithmetic

Immigration day-counting is civil-date arithmetic. "The day you entered Spain"
is a calendar day, not an instant. `new Date('2025-03-01')` is UTC midnight,
which is 2025-02-28 in `America/Mexico_City`; that hour turns a lawful 90-day
Schengen stay into a 91-day overstay on a report a border officer reads.

Use `@meridian/core`: `addDays`, `addMonths` (clamps to month end), `addYears`,
`diffDays`, `compareDates`, `dateRange`, `rangeLengthDays`, `rangeContains`,
`intersectRanges`, `overlapDays`, `mergeRanges` (merges adjacent too),
`totalDays`, `complementRanges`, `calendarYearRange`, `lookbackWindow`,
`eachDay`.

`DateRange` is **closed and inclusive at both ends**. `rangeLengthDays` is
`diffDays + 1`. `lookbackWindow(end, 180)` starts at `end - 179`.

**No package reads a clock.** The one sanctioned read under `packages/` is
`todayUtc()` in `@meridian/mrtd`, present so callers can override it. Two reads
exist under `apps/`, each documented at the top of its file:
`apps/api/src/clock.ts` delegates its civil date to `todayUtc()` and separately
reads an *instant* for audit stamps only (an audit event needs a moment, not a
calendar day, because two events on the same day need an order — it must never
be truncated to ten characters and used as a civil date); and
`apps/admin/lib/clock.ts` reproduces the same UTC civil-date read once, because
`@meridian/mrtd` is not a dependency of that app, with `?asOf=` and
`MERIDIAN_ASOF` overriding it in that order. `apps/web` and `apps/landing` read
no clock — the nationality tool makes its reference date an editable field
rather than a hidden `new Date()`, so every figure it shows can be reproduced
later by anyone who knows the date it was run for. Do not add a third.

`scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs` reads a clock once, in a reporting script, only to
label the report; `--as-of` and `MERIDIAN_ASOF` override it so a report can be
reproduced exactly.

→ `docs/adr/0001-civil-date-arithmetic.md`

### 2. Every applied rule carries a `Citation`

```ts
interface Citation {
  id: string; kind: SourceKind; instrument: string; provision?: string;
  url?: string; jurisdiction: string; verifiedOn: IsoDate;
  discretionary?: boolean; note?: string;
}
```

- `verifiedOn` means a **human opened the source and read it**. Never bump it
  for a citation you did not open — that single act destroys the value of the
  whole field.
- `discretionary: true` where the rule is administrative practice, a screening
  criterion, or a published operational equivalence rather than statutory text.
  Absent-where-it-should-be-present is the dangerous direction: it presents
  practice as settled law.
- A wrong pin-cite is worse than none. Leave `provision` empty rather than
  guessing. Same for `url`.
- Staleness: `fresh` ≤90d, `aging` ≤180d, `stale` >180d.
- **An instrument name is never translated.** It is the identity of a source.
  "Código Civil art. 22.1" rendered as "Civil Code art. 22.1" names a thing that
  does not exist and cannot be looked up by the person trying to check the rule
  that governs their life. `instrumentLang()` in `@meridian/i18n` resolves the
  language an instrument name is in, independently of the UI locale, and returns
  `null` when it does not know — Canada, Quebec and the EU enact in more than
  one authoritative language, and a confident wrong `lang` on a statute is worse
  than an absent one.

→ `docs/adr/0005-data-driven-pathway-catalog.md`,
`docs/LEGAL_CATALOG_REVIEW.md`

### 3. Every engine output is born disclosure-classified

| Class | Definition |
|---|---|
| `information` | Neutral restatement of a published rule, cited, not applied to the user |
| `assessment` | The user's own facts measured against a cited rule, arithmetic shown |
| `advice` | A recommendation, ranking, strategy, or prediction of outcome |

Classification is assigned **where the value is produced**, never at render
time, and travels in `Disclosable<T>` with the citation ids it rests on.
`canRelease(classification, context)` is the single gate: `information` and
`assessment` always pass; `advice` passes to a `practitioner` or
`platform_operator`; `advice` to an `applicant` or `corporate_sponsor` requires
a live, unexpired, jurisdiction-matched `AuthorizedRepresentative`, and is
otherwise **downgraded to `assessment`** with a reason.

`RepresentativeCredential` covers `rcic`, `canadian_lawyer`,
`canadian_paralegal`, `quebec_notary`, `spanish_abogado`, `spanish_gestor` and
`other_regulated`. The paralegal limb of IRPA s.91 is a first-class member
rather than a residual case, because omitting it would wrongly downgrade advice
a licensed professional is in fact accountable for.

Operative test: **anything that ranks options, orders them, scores them, or says
what someone should do is `advice`.** A sort order is a recommendation. So is a
percentage chance of success — and that one would be fabricated besides.

An `assessment` or `advice` with an empty `citationIds` is a defect.

Why: s.91 of Canada's IRPA makes advising for consideration an offence absent an
authorised representative; Spain has reserved-activity exposure for
*asesoramiento jurídico*. Meridian is deliberately **stricter than the
statute** — it downgrades whether or not the reader is paying. The commercial
consequence is written down: the advice boundary and the pricing boundary are
the same boundary, so what is free is decided by IRPA s.91 rather than by us.

→ `docs/adr/0002-advice-boundary-as-a-type.md`, `docs/REGULATORY_POSTURE.md`,
`docs/COMMERCIAL_POSTURE.md`

---

## One page, one language

Not a fourth invariant, but the rule most likely to be broken by an agent
working from an older revision, because the old shape looked deliberate and was
defended in a comment.

Every page used to render English and Spanish into the same elements, through a
`bi()` helper with 1,673 call sites across 61 files. The comment defending it
argued that a mixed-language household should see both halves at once. **The
reasoning was wrong.** A screen-reader user heard every sentence twice. The
document was about twice as long as it needed to be, and every reader paid
scanning cost to discard half of it. `<html lang>` could not be correct, because
the document was two languages at once — and `lang` is the first thing a screen
reader, a hyphenation engine and a search index all read. Per-half `lang`
attributes fixed pronunciation and nothing else.

The resolution:

- **Locale is in the URL.** English unprefixed, Spanish at `/es`, both
  statically prerendered, with `hreflang` alternates and `x-default`. Routes
  live under `app/[locale]/` in all three Next applications. A `beforeFiles`
  rewrite in `next.config.mjs` serves the `/en` route at `/`; a permanent
  redirect sends `/en` and `/en/:path*` back to the unprefixed form, so one
  document does not answer at two addresses and split its own search ranking.
- **`middleware.ts` refuses every other address** — `/fr`, `/EN`, `/es-MX` — and
  renders the not-found document of whichever locale the address was under, by
  *rewrite* rather than `notFound()`, so the 404 is a complete prerendered
  document with a correct `lang` before any script runs. `Accept-Language` is
  deliberately not consulted there: the reader's URL said which document they
  wanted, and the URL is the authority.
- **`@meridian/i18n` is the contract** and depends on nothing — not even
  `@meridian/core`. Every one of its functions can run in a client component,
  and a leaf package that reached into `@meridian/pathways` would drag the whole
  catalog and zod into the browser bundle. That has already happened here once:
  a default reference date imported from `catalog-facts` cost 194 kB before a
  leaf module fixed it. The shapes `i18n` needs from other packages are declared
  **structurally**, so real catalog values satisfy them with no import.
- **The path helpers are asymmetric, and that is the point.** English has no
  prefix, so adding and removing a locale are not inverses. Use `localizedPath`,
  `splitLocalePath`, `alternatePaths`. Do not hand-roll `startsWith('/es')`: it
  decides `/estimate` is Spanish. `alternatePaths` returns *paths*, not URLs,
  because three applications have three hostnames and a leaf package has no
  business knowing any of them; the origin is added once, per app.
- **The switcher is a link, not a control.** A server-rendered anchor with a
  real `href` pointing at *this* page in the other language. It works with
  scripting off, it is crawlable, middle-clicking opens a tab, and there is no
  client state to fall out of step with the URL. It must never substitute the
  home page for the current route. Each option carries its **endonym** with a
  matching `lang`, because a control labelled "Spanish" is useless to the person
  who needs it. Not a flag: a flag is a country and a language is not.
- **`negotiateLocale` may decide exactly one thing** — where to send a reader
  who stated no preference — and must never override an explicit locale in a
  URL. Nothing calls it today.
- **Data stays bilingual.** Nothing about this changed `packages/pathways` or
  `packages/atlas`. A `Pathway` still carries `{ en, es }`; the page picks a
  half. `pick` is for validated catalog data; `resolveText` is for anything that
  crossed a network or database boundary and might be missing a half, and it
  reports the defect rather than rendering a blank string as content.
- **Instrument names are exempt.** See invariant 2.

---

## Repository layout

```
packages/core/        the shared contract — civil-date, disclosure, citation,
                      jurisdiction, tenancy, matter, result, errors
packages/mrtd/        ICAO Doc 9303 — bac, check-digit, dates, parse, types,
                      validate. Imports nothing from Meridian.
packages/presence/    ledger, schengen, tax-residency, continuity,
                      work-experience, catalog-meta
packages/pathways/    schema, facts, evaluate, recommend, integrity, catalog/
packages/documents/   language, model, legalisation, translation, freshness,
                      checklist, gaps
packages/govtech/     capability, adapter, credential-guard, handoff, citations,
                      adapters/{clave,dicireg,ircc}
packages/atlas/       types, blocs, corridor, coverage, stock,
                      regions/{africa,americas,asia,europe,oceania}
packages/i18n/        locale, text, negotiate, path, instrument
                      every package builds to dist/ via tsconfig.build.json
apps/api/             Fastify — auth/ disclosure/ repositories/ audit/ routes/
                      http/ services.ts config.ts clock.ts request-context.ts
                      prisma/schema.prisma + prisma/migrations/ · src/main.ts
apps/landing/         marketing site + Schengen calculator, Next.js 15, port 3000
apps/web/             applicant portal, Next.js 15, port 3001
apps/admin/           firm console, Next.js 15, port 3002
                      all three route under app/[locale]/ with middleware.ts
docs/                 PRD, ARCHITECTURE, REGULATORY_POSTURE, COMMERCIAL_POSTURE,
                      LEGAL_CATALOG_REVIEW, COUNSEL_REVIEW_PACKET, PERSONAS,
                      research/, adr/README + adr/0001-0006
scripts/              check-advice-boundary · check-no-credential-custody
                      check-pathway-citations · check-workspace-manifests
                      (the CI policy job) + atlas-coverage (a report, not a guard)
infra/k8s/production/ namespace, four deployment/service pairs, kustomization,
                      secrets-template (deliberately not a kustomize resource)
enclii.yaml           five documents: a project record + four Services
Dockerfile.{api,web,admin,landing} · docker-compose.yml (Postgres only)
.github/workflows/    ci.yml (policy · typecheck · test · build)
                      build-deploy.yml (builds and signs four images)
```

Dependency direction is one-way with no cycles: `core` ← `presence`, `pathways`,
`documents`, `govtech`; `pathways` ← `documents`. **`mrtd`, `atlas` and `i18n`
depend on nothing.**

The deployed names do not match the directory names, on purpose:
`apps/web` → service `meridian-app` on `meridian-app.madfam.io`, while the
workspace package stays `@meridian/web`, the source stays `apps/web`, the image
stays `meridian-web` and the Janua `client_id` stays `meridian-web`. See
`ECOSYSTEM.md`, and the comments in `infra/k8s/production/web-deployment.yaml`
and `kustomization.yaml`, before changing any of them.

### Boundaries not to cross

- **`packages/core` is the contract.** Changing it changes every package. Do not
  add a helper there while working in a domain package.
- **The evaluator is law-free.** `packages/pathways/src/evaluate.ts` contains no
  country name, threshold or legal concept — 22 operations over plain data.
  Adding a jurisdiction is a new file in `src/catalog/`. A legal rule in the
  evaluator has escaped to a place no reviewing lawyer will look.
- **A package's `src/index.ts` is its only public surface.** The `exports` map
  has one entry, `"."`, with `types` at `./dist/index.d.ts` and `default` at
  `./dist/index.js`. Consumers import **emitted JavaScript**, not TypeScript
  source. Raw engines behind a disclosure wrapper are unreachable from outside on
  purpose; do not widen it "for testing", and do not point a default condition
  back at `src/`.
- **No engine package ever sees a repository or performs I/O.**
- **`@meridian/i18n` must not gain a dependency.** It runs in client components.
- **The catalog order is a legal constraint, not a style choice.**
  `MERIDIAN_PATHWAY_CATALOG` is the concatenation of `MERIDIAN_CATALOG_MODULES`
  in a fixed, append-stable order, so `evaluateAll` and `assess` return reports
  in an order that says nothing about merit, likelihood or priority — a ranking
  is advice, and only `recommend()` may produce one. Sorting by id was rejected
  because renaming a slug would reshuffle what every reader sees first; sorting
  by anything substantive would be a claim about importance. New modules go on
  the end of their jurisdiction's block; new pathways go on the end of their
  module's array. Appending never renumbers an existing record.

### A new workspace package breaks every image

Adding a package leaves it out of the lockfile and out of all four Dockerfiles,
so CI's root install fails on `--frozen-lockfile` — and the failure names the
lockfile rather than the missing `COPY`, while the image builds keep passing
against the pre-change lockfile, which makes the whole thing look like an
infrastructure flake. This has happened twice, once for `apps/landing` and once
for `packages/atlas`. `Dockerfile.api` carried a comment saying exactly this, in
capitals, directly above the `COPY` block; it was not enough. A comment is not a
control, so the rule is now `scripts/check-workspace-manifests.mjs`, and it runs
in the policy job before any install — the install being the thing it predicts.

### Why the packages emit JavaScript

They did not always. The packages once published `"main": "./src/index.ts"` and
shipped no build step, which is correct inside the workspace — `tsc` and vitest
read the sources directly — and fatal in a container: Node executes JavaScript
and its type-stripping mode does not remap the `./x.js` specifiers those files
use onto the `./x.ts` files on disk. An image built that way starts and dies on
its first import, in production, after a green pipeline. So each package now
builds with `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` and `Dockerfile.api` imports every
package under Node before it will emit an image.

Two consequences to preserve:

- Turbo's `typecheck` and `test` both `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, so a cross-package
  import always reads a fresh `dist/`. A stale `dist` means you are testing code
  you did not write.
- `transpilePackages` and `experimental.extensionAlias` have been **removed** from
  all three Next configs, and each config records why. There are no `.ts` files
  inside `@meridian/*` for webpack to compile, and remapping `./civil-date.js`
  onto `civil-date.ts` would send a valid JavaScript request hunting for
  TypeScript that is not published. Restoring either would break `next build`.

---

## TypeScript and testing contract

Strict: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`,
`verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, `noImplicitReturns`,
`noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`. ESM. Target ES2022, `lib: ES2022`,
`moduleResolution: Bundler`.

- Relative imports **must** end in `.js`.
- Type-only imports **must** use `import type`.
- Expected failures return `Result<T, E>`. "Ineligible" is a value, not an
  exception. `MeridianError` with a stable `code` for genuine faults and untyped
  boundaries.
- No `TODO` for core functionality. No "not implemented" throw. No mock data.
- Doc comments explain **why**, especially where the reason is legal. Match the
  density and voice of `packages/core/src`.
- No prettier config exists; existing code runs to roughly 100-110 columns.
  Match the file you are editing.

Tests live in `tests/*.test.ts` (or `.test.tsx` in the Next applications), use
vitest, and target what would actually hurt a person: boundary off-by-ones
(exactly 90 compliant, 91 breaching), leap years and 29 February, empty input,
the difference between absent (`unknown`) and empty array (a positive `false`),
ordering independence via a seeded shuffle, adversarial input (prototype
pollution, a host parsing as the wrong half of a URL, data on the prototype
chain), and timezone traps.

Prefer a test that cross-checks against an independent recomputation over one
that restates the implementation.

**Beware green-by-vacuity.** Two instances are on record here and both shipped:
a readiness probe whose `SELECT 1` proved a socket and not a schema, and two
tool routes whose components existed without a `page.tsx`, so Next built no
route, emitted no error, and `pnpm build` went green having built less than
intended — two 404s reached production behind a passing check. A verification
that asks "did the command exit 0" is not the same as one that asks "does the
thing I expected exist". The four guards each print what they examined for the
same reason.

---

## Verification commands

From any project directory — the eight `packages/<name>` and the four `apps/*`
all carry suites:

```bash
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm exec vitest run
```

Both must exit clean. Never report success without having run them and seen
them pass. If your change moves a test count, state the new number.

Across packages — build first, because packages are consumed as emitted
JavaScript:

```bash
pnpm build --filter "./packages/*"
pnpm -r --filter "./packages/*" typecheck
pnpm -r --filter "./packages/*" test
```

Whole repo, which is what CI runs:

```bash
pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build
```

And the four policy guards, which need no install and are the fastest signal
that an invariant broke rather than a build:

```bash
node scripts/check-advice-boundary.mjs
node scripts/check-no-credential-custody.mjs
node scripts/check-pathway-citations.mjs
node scripts/check-workspace-manifests.mjs
```

Plus the coverage report, which needs the packages built:

```bash
node scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs --as-of=YYYY-MM-DD
```

If you change how a package is built, resolved or exported, also build and run
the API image — it is the only check that catches a package resolving to
TypeScript at runtime:

```bash
docker build -f Dockerfile.api -t meridian-api:local .
docker run --rm meridian-api:local
```

`check-no-credential-custody` scans the whole tree, `docs/` included. When
writing about the credential refusal, **describe** the forbidden field names
rather than spelling them, or the document itself trips the check. Only
`packages/govtech/src/credential-guard.ts`, `packages/govtech/tests/` and the
script are exempt, and each exemption is asserted to still exist.

**Do not run `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` or `npm install`** while another agent
or process may be working in the same worktree — concurrent installs corrupt the
shared store. If you think you need a package that is not present, use the Node
standard library or what is already there, and say so in your report.

---

## Things this repository will not do

- **No custody of government credentials.** No Cl@ve PIN, no Cl@ve Permanente
  password, no portal password, no e.firma key — not stored, not proxied, not
  held in memory for a request. Refused at four layers: capability state
  `refused_by_policy`, `CredentialFree<T>` making the field unrepresentable,
  `guardCredentialFree` at runtime, and `@ts-expect-error` tests so `tsc` fails
  if the refusal breaks. The replacement is `buildHandoff`. The decisive
  argument is attribution, not encryption: a submission made with the user's
  credential is legally *the user's act*, performed by someone else, with no
  record of consent to that act on that day. → `docs/adr/0003-no-credential-custody.md`
- **No advice to an unrepresented applicant.** → `docs/adr/0002-advice-boundary-as-a-type.md`
- **No synthetic success.** No adapter returns a plausible-looking government
  response nobody obtained from a government. `verifyNoSyntheticSuccess()` makes
  it checkable.
- **No ranking from an unreviewed catalog.**
- **No score, percentage or probability of success**, anywhere.
- **No invented law.** Omit, or mark `discretionary: true` with a note saying
  counsel must verify.
- **No asylum, refugee or humanitarian/compassionate route in the catalog**, in
  any jurisdiction, ever.

---

## Ecosystem contract

- **Auth**: Janua. Verify JWTs via JWKS at
  `https://auth.madfam.io/.well-known/jwks.json`. **RS256 only**; HS256 and
  `alg: none` fail closed (2026-04-23 audit, H3/H4).
- **Billing**: Dhanam — tenant entitlements and metering.
- **Inference**: Selva at `/v1`, OpenAI-compatible. **Every LLM call routes
  here, never a provider directly.** No provider SDK belongs in this repo.
- **Compliance**: Karafiel — NOM-151 timestamping, the natural home for the
  immutable audit trail of release decisions.
- **Legal corpus**: Tezca — Mexican-law oracle, informational.
- **Deploy**: Enclii. `enclii onboard --repo madfam-org/meridian`.
- **CORS**: explicit allowlist per service; wildcards banned (H2/H5/H6), and
  rejected by `apps/api/src/config.ts` at load rather than at use.
- **Images**: `@sha256:`-pinned in every manifest.
- **Dates**: ISO 8601 everywhere; times in `America/Mexico_City`.

Namespace `meridian`. `meridian-landing` :3000 on meridian.madfam.io,
`meridian-app` :3000 on meridian-app.madfam.io, `meridian-admin` :3000 on
meridian-admin.madfam.io — all three answering `200` on 2026-07-26 — and
`meridian-api` :8000 on meridian-api.madfam.io, answering `502`. Registry
`ghcr.io/madfam-org/` with two path shapes — `meridian-api`, `meridian-web`,
`meridian-admin` from before the landing split and the nested `meridian/landing`
after it. Container ports are framework defaults and have no production effect:
pods have their own network namespaces and the tunnel routes by hostname. The
port is named `http` throughout so containerPort, Service targetPort, probes and
the generated NetworkPolicy agree by construction. No port block is claimed.
Local dev uses 3000/3001/3002 and whatever `PORT` says for the API.
`ECOSYSTEM.md` carries the full argument — reference it rather than restating it.

**The `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` set has been removed.** Forty declarations across the
Dockerfiles, manifests and CI were read by zero lines of source. Configuration
that lies is worse than absent configuration: it tells the next engineer a
wiring exists when it does not. `grep -rn NEXT_PUBLIC apps packages` matches
nothing, and each former site carries a comment saying why. Reintroduce them in
the change that makes an application read them, not before.

## Enclii-first operations contract

Use Enclii web, API, or CLI for routine production provisioning, deployment,
observability, domain management, secrets, provider operations, scaling,
rollback and remediation.

Raw `kubectl`, `helm`, SSH, provider CLIs/APIs, `docker exec` and direct
container access are allowed only for platform bootstrap or documented
break-glass emergencies when Enclii is unavailable or lacks an implemented
adapter. Any break-glass use must record the actor, reason, target service and
environment, commands executed, result, and the follow-up adapter gap or
incident link.

Meridian raises the bar: a break-glass session here can reach passport,
biometric-derived and travel-history data. Treat it as a data-access event, not
only an operational one.

---

## Data sensitivity

This platform is designed to process travel-document data, biometric-derived
data (the ICAO BAC key seed), multi-year travel history, immigration status
including prior refusals and removals, criminal-record certificate status, and
income data.

Under GDPR, parts of that corpus are **Article 9 special-category** (biometric
data for unique identification; nationality data from which racial or ethnic
origin can be inferred) and criminal-record data falls under **Article 10**.
Mexican LFPDPPP treats several categories as *datos personales sensibles*. The
entire corpus is treated at the special-category standard.

**This repository is PUBLIC.** No secrets, no credentials, no real personal
data, no real MRZ strings — not in code, tests, fixtures, issues, pull requests
or commit messages. Every fixture is synthetic: issuing state `ZZZ`, document
numbers beginning `ZZ`, `example.invalid` hostnames.

Vulnerabilities go to **security@madfam.io**, never to a public issue.

→ `SECURITY.md`

---

## Repo-boundary contract

Meridian is **Lane C — a public service repo**. It carries public-safe service
documentation only.

- `internal-devops` (private) — secrets, credentials, cluster access, server
  identity, cost ledgers, incident records, operator gates, full runbooks.
- `solarpunk-foundry` (public) — the ecosystem contract hub.
- Meridian (public) — service-specific implementation guidance, public-safe
  status and operational contracts, sanitized references to `internal-devops`.

Every new public document needs a one-line boundary note with a canonical link.
When uncertain about placement, default to `internal-devops` and leave a
public-safe summary plus a link here.

---

## Known gaps carried forward

Recorded so no agent mistakes them for a decision:

1. No contract test suite for the repository ports. The in-memory and Prisma
   adapters can drift, and ADR 0006 names that as its main risk.
2. The initial migration exists at `apps/api/prisma/migrations/` and nothing in
   the deploy path runs it. It has never been applied to a live Postgres.
3. Nothing has been exercised end to end; no request has travelled from a screen
   through the service to a database in any environment.
4. `meridian-api.madfam.io` returns `502`. Operator gates outstanding.
5. No pathway is counsel-reviewed. Legal review is the gating item between the
   engine and a sellable product.
6. `@meridian/atlas` has no consumer inside the product — only
   `scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs` and its own tests read it.
7. `negotiateLocale` is implemented and tested and called by nothing.
8. The source PRD text is not committed; `docs/PRD.md` holds the editorial
   preface, the record of our departures and a marked block awaiting the
   verbatim origin document.
9. `packages/mrtd/package.json` declares no dependencies while `src/bac.ts`
   imports `node:crypto`. Types resolve from the hoisted root `@types/node`, so
   `tsc` is clean today. Add `"@types/node": "^22.10.2"` to that package's
   devDependencies the next time the lockfile is touched. There is no runtime
   dependency — `node:crypto` is standard library.
10. No formatting check. Prettier is a root devDependency with no config file
    and CI does not run it.
11. Data residency for EU subjects is an open architectural question.
12. Document storage and presence-ledger ingestion are undesigned.

## Maintenance

`AGENTS.md` is canonical; `CLAUDE.md` is a redirect. If repo-specific long-form
agent guidance is needed, it goes in `AGENTS.md`, not `CLAUDE.md`. These context
files are hand-curated for this repository — if the ecosystem doc-sync tooling
offers to regenerate them, read the diff before accepting it.

Every status figure in this file decays. The ones most likely to be wrong first
are the test counts, the deployment table and the catalog totals. Re-measure
before quoting: `pnpm test`, a request to each hostname, and
`node scripts/check-pathway-citations.mjs`.
